current.text: His toe injury from last season is reportedly healed.
He is projected to come off the bench. Ty Jerome is the starting point guard and started both preseason games.
He is likely the sixth man, competing with Jaylen Wells for bench minutes and with Jerome for point guard minutes.
He has been working at shooting guard, so he could start next to Jerome.
He would be a must add everywhere if Jerome gets hurt and Pippen moves into the starting lineup.
Experts disagree on drafting him. One says he is ranked too low and is a late-round swing pick and deep-bench stash. A newer take says nothing in preseason makes drafting him make sense.
Memphis is expected to use an 11 or 12 man rotation with short, hard stints and a high pace, which keeps bench minutes down.
Memphis has a maxed 4-4-4 schedule in our playoff weeks through March 28 and only 13 back-to-backs, possibly the fewest in the league.

durable.text: Steals are his standout category, far above the top 250 pool. Assists are his other positive category.
He is a strong perimeter defender.
He is less useful in points leagues than in category leagues.

note: He ranks 166 on Yahoo and 134 on ESPN, and both sites price him at about 0 USD. With only 144 players drafted, he sits at the edge of our draft pool, so he costs at most 1 USD as a last bench pick for builds that chase steals and assists. Early in the season, check his minutes against Jaylen Wells and Ty Jerome's health, because a starting role would make him a must add.
